description:
FOUND s502e (Opus, 2026-10-04) shipping #2056 (File::Temp->new; a lexical handle's `*$fh` is now a per-stream anonymous glob, %p-stream-glob).  Two cells of the glob-as-object table stay wrong, and the anonymous glob has a lifetime cost.

(1) `*$fh{IO}` answers the glob (class GLOB) for a lexical handle AND for `*STDOUT{IO}`; perl gives an IO::File object.  PRE-EXISTING (base e5d72352 identical).
(2) `"" . *{$fh}` stringifies as `*pcl-anonio::__anonio__N` (base: `GLOB(0x…)`); perl gives `*main::$fh` -- the declaring lexical's NAME, which PCL does not carry at run time.
REPRODUCER (scratch/s502e/p/glob2.pl in the s502e worktree):
    open(my $fh, "<", "/etc/hostname") or die;
    print "io ", ref(*$fh{IO}), "\n";                                          # perl IO::File   PCL GLOB
    my $s = "" . *{$fh}; $s =~ s/0x[0-9a-f]+/ADDR/; print "str $s\n";           # perl *main::$fh  PCL *pcl-anonio::__anonio__1
    print "io2 ", ref(*STDOUT{IO}), "\n";                                       # perl IO::File   PCL GLOB
(3) LIFETIME: %p-stream-glob registers the anonymous glob's NAME in *p-filehandles* (name -> stream) so `fileno(*$fh)`, `print {*$fh}` and `*$fh{IO}` resolve it -- that entry is a STRONG reference to the stream, so the weak *p-stream-globs* entry for a `*`-dereferenced lexical handle (and the stream struct, its glob and the glob's slot cells) is never collected.  One entry per File::Temp object / IO::Socket handle whose `*$fh` was touched; bounded in a script, unbounded in a long-lived image.  CHEAP MEASUREMENT: loop 100k `{ open my $fh, "<", "/etc/hostname"; ${*$fh}{k} = 1; close $fh }` and print (hash-table-count pcl::*p-filehandles*) via a debug hook, or watch RSS.  FIX SHAPE: remhash the synthetic name in the close path (p-close already resolves the stream), or give p-typeglob an optional STREAM slot so the anonymous glob needs no name registration at all.

Everyday/board impact: none known (the File-Temp everyday row is `same` with #2056).
subject: Glob-as-object residue after #2056: *$fh{IO} is GLOB not IO::File (also *STDOUT{IO}), "*{$fh}" stringifies *pcl-anonio::__anonio__N not *main::$fh, and the anonymous glob of a *-dereferenced lexical handle is never collected (name registered strongly in *p-filehandles*)
